scope: 2025 Rhode Island General Assembly members; the site displays an entry only when name, chamber, and district match a 2026 candidate.
methodology: RIEP displays third-party legislative measures only with clear attribution and a source link. Organization-created numerical scores are reproduced only when the organization itself publishes a legislator-specific score. Voting records that do not publish an overall score, including the ACLU of Rhode Island's 2025 record, are displayed as voting records and are not converted by RIEP into percentages, grades, rankings, or composite assessments. Measures from different organizations are not combined or normalized. State Legislative Effectiveness Scores from the Center for Effective Lawmaking are displayed separately as a research measure.

research_audit.organization: Center for Effective Lawmaking (University of Virginia and Vanderbilt University)
research_audit.latest_reviewed: 2023–2024 Rhode Island State Legislative Effectiveness Scores
research_audit.reason: Nonpartisan research measure of legislators' demonstrated ability to advance sponsored bills through the legislative process. Displayed separately from advocacy-group voting scorecards.

research_audit.organization: Rhode Island League of Cities and Towns
research_audit.reason: Current statewide scorecard with explicit legislator-by-legislator numerical scores for both chambers.

Included as an attributed voting record, not as an RIEP score. The ACLU selected 11 Senate roll calls and identified its preferred position on each. RIEP links to the original record and does not calculate a percentage, grade, rank, or overall civil-liberties assessment.

The state legislative scorecard page located in this audit currently surfaces 2021-2022. It is retained as a research source but excluded from the current 2026 candidate rating display because of age.

research_audit.organization: Rhode Island Center for Freedom & Prosperity
research_audit.latest_reviewed: Rhode Island Freedom Index / interactive scorecard
research_audit.reason: The Center publishes an ideologically framed Freedom Index, but the current public pages located in this audit point to older scorecard cycles rather than a verified 2025-2026 statewide legislator table. RIEP does not substitute an old score for a current one.

The current NAACP Civil Rights Scorecard located in this audit is a federal U.S. Senate scorecard, not a Rhode Island General Assembly scorecard, so it is not applicable to state legislative candidate profiles.

The current scorecard located is from the League of Women Voters of Maine; no current Rhode Island General Assembly legislator scorecard with candidate-by-candidate numerical ratings was verified in this audit.
